Keywords: Sacred book gold pigments and patrons
RagShortTexts: Decorated books require scribes, pigments and patronage.
Gold decoration and binding add time and expense.

Variants.Content: A decorated sacred book needs planned spaces for script and pictures, then writing, painting, gold work and binding. Worship and a patron’s standing are linked. Costly materials make mistakes and transport damage painful; several craftspeople contribute to one volume.
When escorting a sacred book, sound packing and dry storage matter more than displaying gold. Crushing the spine or soaking its chest damages text needed for worship as well as wealth.
A sacred-book commission displays piety and standing. Promised gold still needs scribes and liturgical planning; premature presentation dates turn patronage into debt or broken promises.
Painters, scribes and binders depend on one another’s work. Limited gold can mean less decoration, but replacing a ruined leaf also discards the labor already invested in it.
